newsitem.title: UK: Italy low sulphur fuel use falls in Jan year/year.
newsitem.headline: Italy low sulphur fuel use falls in Jan year/year.

text.p: Italian consumption of low sulphur fuel oil for power generation was 1.15 million tonnes in January, a 33.1 percent fall from January last year, Italian industry group Unione Petrolifera said on Thursday.

Italy's total consumption of low sulphur fuel oil, including that for non-power industrial use, was 1.34 million tonnes in January, a fall of just over 30 percent compared to January 1996, the data added.

But total Italian consumption of high sulphur fuel oil rose by 26 percent to 698,000 tonnes in January meaning that total Italian fuel oil consumption, including that for shipping bunker fuels, was around 18 percent down year-on-year at 2.09 million tonnes.
The data also showed smaller percentage falls in consumption on a monthly basis. Consumption of low sulphur fuel oil by Italy's power sector in January was just 10 percent higher than in December.
Total high and low sulphur fuel oil consumption in January showed a monthly rise of around 2.5 percent.

Data for total Italian imports were not available, a source at Unione Petrolifera said, because Italian state utility ENEL has failed to release up-to-date inventory data, against which imports can be calculated.
Poor demand from ENEL, the world's largest single buyer of fuel oil, has helped knock over 25 percent off the value of European low sulphur fuel oil in two months.
Low sulphur fuel oil dipped below $100 a tonne fob NWE on Wednesday, the first time since August.

The fall in Italy's fuel oil consumption mirrors that of many other European countries as increasingly cheap and abundant supplies of natural gas are piped in from the North Sea and from outside the region.
In addition, hydro electric output in Italy has been higher this winter because of heavy rains.
